messages:
Alex: Heads up — we saw a small skew in priority routing during the last canary. Some cohort users ended up in the cost-optimized pool despite tenant-level quota priority. Spotted ~17:03 UTC.
Maria: Ugh. Is this the tie-breaker fallback problem we thought was closed?
Sam: I pulled logs. When routes tie on priority we fall back to hash(tenant_id) mod N. After the last runtime-config bump the hash seed defaulted to 0 for snapshots missing the field. That caused many tenants to collide.
Jin: Confirmed. The config schema migration didn't backfill seed; our runtime treats missing seed as zero. Older snapshots without seed = lots of identical buckets.
Alex: Impact? severity?
Sam: Roughly 0.3% of requests in the canary window affected. No SLO breach, but quota isolation was wrong for a few customer teams.
Maria: For future rollouts can we gate on snapshot completeness? A preflight that warns or blocks if snapshot fields used by runtime are missing. Also a console flag for snapshots lacking seed.
Jin: My preference: non-blocking warning + background migration. Generate a deterministic derived seed per-tenant (HMAC(tenant_id, global_key)) and write back to snapshot. Avoid runtime interruption.
Alex: Two actionable asks: 1) hotfix runtime to prefer derived HMAC if seed missing (instead of zero), 2) implement snapshot backfill migration.
Sam: Hotfix is straightforward: compute HMAC(tenant_id, migration_key) when seed absent. We must ensure migration_key is stable across nodes — use config-store value.
Maria: Caution: config-store keys are region-scoped. If different keys across regions, derived seeds will differ, causing cross-region routing inconsistency. We need a rollout-safe global key.
Jin: Proposal: add migration_key to runtime-config with explicit rollouts. For safety, the key is introduced via canary; migration job also runs after key is available. In the interim, the runtime will emit a metric indicating seed_source.
Alex: Telemetry: create metric routing.tie_breaker.source with label seed_source={explicit,derived,legacy_zero}. Alert if derived exceeds 0.1% during canary. Add dashboard tile showing seed_source distribution and quota mismatch by tenant.
Sam: I'll add the metric, and a console dashboard showing derived vs explicit counts and any tenants with quota anomalies. Also add a paging rule if legacy_zero spikes >0.5% in 15m.
Maria: UX: console should show a warning icon next to snapshots missing seed. Tooltip: "Derived seed applied; run migration to persist stable seed." Link to runbook. Keep copy friendly: explain derived seeds are deterministic and safe.
Jin: Runbook draft: 1) verify migration_key rollout, 2) schedule low-QPS migration job to backfill seeds, 3) validate by sampling tenants and confirming routing.tie_breaker.source == explicit, 4) turn off legacy_zero fallback.
Alex: Ownership: Sam = telemetry & validation, Jin = migration job implementation, Maria = console UX & runbook text. I'll create tasks in Tracker and assign.
Sam: Ack. I'll instrument, create dashboard, and open alert PR.
Jin: I'll prototype migration in staging against 50k synthetic tenants to measure perf impact and idempotency. Plan a canary run for a subset of snapshots first.
Maria: UX nit: show the migration status per-namespace and estimated completion time. That'll reduce support tickets.
Alex: Timeline proposal: hotfix runtime to compute derived seed today and roll to canary; telemetry + dashboard tomorrow; migration job and console UI next week. Agree?
Sam: Sounds good. I'll send the runtime metric PR now.
Jin: Opening migration RFC and prototype branch.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: rollout/runtime-canary-2026-03-23-2 to canary pool (20%). Checks: unit tests passed, smoke ok.
Alex: After deploy, monitor routing.tie_breaker.source and quota-mismatch logs for 30m and report back here. :thumbsup:
Maria: I'll draft the tooltip copy and add to the console PR for review.
Sam: Runtime metric PR landed in staging — link posted in PR tracker.
Jin: RFC draft: https://r.redwood/runbooks/migrations/tie-breaker-seed-backfill (draft).
Alex: Thanks all. We'll reconvene tomorrow for a short sync if any anomalies show up.
